h1: Which FCO forms does a biostimulant business actually deal with?
title: Which FCO forms does a biostimulant firm need? | GBO
desc: What Forms G, G-1, G-2, G-3, A1, A2 and O are for, who files each one, and which ones lapsed in June 2025 under the Fertiliser Control Order.
answer: A biostimulant manufacturer or importer files Form G to get a product into Schedule VI. Forms G-1, G-2 and G-3 belonged to the provisional route, now closed. Selling is a separate state step: the authorisation letter, with Forms A1, A2 and O in the older Order text. Check with your state agriculture department.
sections: The seven papers at a glance

There are two tracks. One asks whether the product is allowed at all, and runs through the Controller and Schedule VI. The other asks whether this firm may sell in this state, and runs through the state.

PaperGoes to or comes fromWhat it is forStatus to keep in mind
Form GManufacturer or importer applies to the ControllerGetting a biostimulant included in Schedule VI, with supporting dataThe current route for a product not yet listed
Form G-1Existing maker applied to the ControllerAsking for provisional registrationProvisional route is closed
Form G-2Issued by the State Government, signed by the Director of AgricultureCertifying prior sale and no reported complaint, to support G-1Provisional route is closed
Form G-3Issued by the ControllerThe certificate of provisional registrationInvalid since 17 June 2025
Form A1Seller files with the state Notified AuthorityMemorandum of Intimation to sellRead in an older copy of the Order
Form A2Notified Authority gives it backAcknowledgement, treated as the authorisation letterRead in an older copy of the Order
Form OIssued by the source of supplyCertificate of source: shows where the goods came fromRead in an older copy of the Order

Clause 20C and Forms G-2 and G-3 are read here as reproduced in a Delhi High Court judgment of 18 August 2025. Forms A1, A2 and O are read in an older consolidated copy of the Order on an Odisha government site. That copy stops before the 2021 changes. Check with your state agriculture department.
Form G: what getting into Schedule VI asks for

Clause 20C(3) says every manufacturer or importer of a biostimulant shall apply to the Controller in Form G. A marketer who only sells under its own brand is not named in that sub-clause.

The data headings in the clause, as the court reproduced them, are:

  • Chemistry: the source of the material, the product specification with laboratory analysis, the method of analysis, and shelf-life.
  • Bio-efficacy trials: agronomic trials of the product.
  • Toxicity: acute toxicity and eco-toxicity tests.
  • Heavy metal analysis report, with the product also not laced with pesticide beyond the limit in the clause.

A proviso covers biostimulants of natural origin. For those, the data required is as decided by the Central Biostimulants Committee. So a seaweed or plant extract applicant should find out what the committee decided, not assume.

One warning. The judgment records a submission that a Fifth Amendment Order notified on 9 June 2025 provides for bio-efficacy trials and the method of testing. We have not opened that Gazette text, so we give no trial design here. Read the latest Gazette before planning any trial. Check with your state agriculture department.
Forms G-1, G-2 and G-3: the provisional route

When biostimulants came under the Order through S.O. 882(E) of 23 February 2021, products were already on sale. Sub-clause 20C(4) let existing makers carry on for two years, if they applied under the next sub-clause.

  • Form G-1 was that application, with details of the product, its specifications, label and other particulars. The judgment names this form but does not print it, so we say no more about its contents.
  • Form G-2 was the state certificate. It said the firm had sold the named product before the notification and that no complaint of ill or hazardous effects had been reported.
  • Form G-3 was the provisional certificate from the Controller. It named the maker, product, place of manufacture and storage.

The Government's release of 9 September 2025 says G-3 certificates went to more than 8,000 products. Validity first ended on 23 February 2023, was extended to 22 February 2024, 22 February 2025 and 16 June 2025, and the registrations stand invalid since 17 June 2025. The same release says 146 products were in Schedule VI as of September 2025. Later amendments have added more, so check the latest Gazette list.

The Delhi High Court allowed some firms with pending or deficient Schedule VI applications to operate until a decision. That relief was limited to members of the petitioner associations and the other named petitioners. It is not a general extension, and rejected applicants got no such room. The sources we read do not say what happens to old stock, so we do not guess. Check with your state agriculture department.
Forms A1, A2 and O: the right to sell

Product status and the right to sell are separate papers. Condition 4 of Form G-3 said that, for selling a biostimulant, the authorisation letter shall be obtained from the Notified Authority of the concerned State Government.

The older text of clause 8 explains how a fertiliser seller gets that letter:

  • Every person who intends to sell, including a manufacturer, importer, wholesaler or retail dealer, files a Form A1 Memorandum of Intimation in duplicate, with the fee.
  • A Form O certificate of source goes with it. The source can be a manufacturer, importer or wholesale dealer, among others.
  • The Notified Authority acknowledges in Form A2, which is deemed to be the authorisation letter. Clause 10 of that text gives authorisation letters three years, unless renewed, suspended or cancelled.

Be careful with the join. The text we read does not say in so many words that a biostimulant takes this exact path today. It does show that states look for these papers: Bihar's online checklist for G-3 certified biostimulants asks for the source or Form O in original, and an appointment letter for the responsible person under clause 24. That checklist was built around G-3, so it may change.

For a private-label marketer, the practical point is Form O. It is the paper that links your stock to your source, and it comes from your supplier. Check with your state agriculture department.

There are two uses of Form G. In the older text, clause 15(2) uses Form G for a certificate of manufacture for a special fertiliser mixture. In clause 20C, Form G is the biostimulant inclusion application.

A G-3 is not a current approval. A supplier who still shows a G-3 as proof of approval is showing a lapsed paper. Ask instead which Schedule VI entry the grade falls under. The Schedule VI page explains how to check.

Schedule VI lists the product, not your firm. A Lok Sabha answer of August 2024 said every manufacturer can now manufacture any biostimulant specified in Schedule VI. Clause 20C(8) also provides for the names of manufacturers or importers of included biostimulants to be published in the Gazette. Neither says the state step goes away. Check with your state agriculture department.

For what goes on the pack and in the file, use our label and documents checklist.
Where a manufacturer fits in this paperwork

Gujarat Bio Organics makes at its own plant at GIDC Shihor, Bhavnagar, with capacity of 100 KL liquid and 2,500 t solid a month. We have worked with farmers since 2006. We hold Gujarat NOCs for 36 FCO Schedule VI biostimulant grades and 11 biofertiliser types.

A NOC is a state paper. It is not one of the forms above, and the clause text we read does not define it. So match each product to a grade on the supplier's NOC, and ask how the rules apply in the state where the goods will be sold. That goes for any supplier, including us. Check with your state agriculture department.
faq: Which form gets a new biostimulant into Schedule VI?

Form G, filed by the manufacturer or importer with the Controller, with data on chemistry, bio-efficacy, toxicity and heavy metals, as clause 20C(3) sets out. A later amendment may have changed some of this, so read the latest Gazette and check with your state agriculture department.
Is a Form G-3 still valid?
No. The Government says provisional registrations stand invalid since 17 June 2025. Check with your state agriculture department.
Does a brand owner who does not manufacture file Form G?
Clause 20C(3) names manufacturers and importers only. A marketer still needs the right to sell in its state. Check with your state agriculture department.
It is the certificate of source. In the older text of the Order it shows where fertiliser for sale was obtained, and it goes with the Form A1 memorandum. Check with your state agriculture department.
Does Schedule VI listing replace state authorisation?
No text we read says so. Form G-3 itself required an authorisation letter from the state for selling. Check with your state agriculture department.
